fields.name: Cash Data Management
fields.description: Tools delivering the basic functionalities needed to carry out a Cash program: beneficiary registration, distribution, reconciliation, feedback & surveys, and reporting & analytics.

fields.title: Cost
fields.description: There are costs associated with setting up and maintaining a tool throughout the program implementation lifecycle.
fields.label_1: No funding is likely to be raised or allocated for this. We are looking primarily for a very low cost or free solution (or mix of solutions) that will allow our team to manage data without paying much for either the set up or maintenance. Ideally we would find a tool that doesn't have any sort of cost to license, host, or use.
fields.label_2: We will have funding to cover minimal cost to configure and use the solution for a limited time or volume. The tool needs to have clear pricing that will allow us to estimate the total cost to run and maintain it for the life of our program.
fields.label_3: We will have funding to cover some expenses related to the configuration and use of the tool for our program. While we prefer to keep costs low, we may have some flexibility if a given solution meets multiple of our needs.
fields.label_4: We will have funding to cover the higher cost of a fully-featured solution, and a plan to fund it for as long as we will use it. We can pay more if the tool can handle a variety of functions that we might otherwise pay separately for. The larger investment may be justified by the size of the operation, or by plans to continue to use the tool for other programs and operations.

fields.title: Setup Time
fields.description: Teams frequently face deadlines for getting a tool up and running, and there are a variety of factors that can impact the time it takes.
fields.label_1: We don't have much time. Spinning up an instance of the tool must be done in a matter of hours, and tweaking it to meet our needs has to be a matter of pointing and clicking through a simple interface.
fields.label_2: We are in a rush, but have at least a few days to handle the configuration, including building out the data fields to match the program.
fields.label_3: We have some flexibility and at least a week before we need the tool up and running. Setup can be slow due to dependencies outside of our control, and we have time to consult necessary technical experts that might need to help with the configuration process.
fields.label_4: We have lots of flexibility to ensure that we take the time needed to carefully configure the tool. We have two weeks or more to be very deliberate with the set up process.

fields.title: Setup Complexity
fields.description: Tools require varying levels of technical experience to configure them to suit the program's needs. Some may offer "off-the-shelf" functionality while others might require more advanced Information Management skills like coding to properly get the tool working.
fields.label_1: We need a solution that is very easy to set up and that requires no special technical skills. The tool should be pre-configured or come from a vendor whose price includes this step.
fields.label_2: Our team is able to do basic configuration including processes that might rely on intermediate knowledge of formulas and spreadsheet manipulation, but but not coding or advanced processes.
fields.label_3: We have specialist support on a limited basis that can complete complicated set up and configuration, for example coding, database management, or similarly-advanced technical processes.
fields.label_4: We have dedicated specialist support for the duration of our program that can complete complicated set up and configuration, for example coding, database management, or similarly-advanced technical processes.

fields.title: Maintenance
fields.description: While setting up a tool may bring certain technical challenges, we cannot overlook the importance of considering the time, money, and human resourcing necessary to keep the tool up and running.
fields.label_1: We do not have resources to manage and maintain the tool, our team needs to focus solely on program implementation. This must be handled automatically or by the vendor.
fields.label_2: While we prefer a tool that is simple to maintain, we do have some resources available to manage the tool after it has been set up. That doesn't mean we can tinker with computer code or other technically-intensive tasks, but we can make small changes to the configuration as needs arise.
fields.label_3: We need a tool that can be adjusted as the program is carried out, and have at least one person on our team that can handle relatively straightforward maintenance tasks or configuration adjustments.
fields.label_4: Our team has a dedicated and highly-capable technology specialist that will have the time available to provide ongoing support as needed when any maintenance tasks, required updates, or configuration adjsutments arise.

fields.title: Train Learn
fields.description: When configuring the tool, using the tool, and training users, we will inevitably run into issues that will require consulting some sort of documentation or online support. More widely used tools may provide extensive technical documentation and entire online communities dedicated to providing support, while more niche tools may lack these resources.
fields.label_1: We're looking for a tool that is extremely well-documented, with extensive online resources that cover everything from setup and configuration to overcoming technical challenges for specific features we want. My end users also need access to some sort of support network or resource that can quickly answer their questions.
fields.label_2: We don't necessarily need a bunch of resources like online user support forums or blogs that outline use cases similar to mine, but having good documentation and other available support resources would be very desirable.
fields.label_3: At the very minimum, we need a user's manual for how to get the tool set up. We can figure out how to adapt it to my our use-case's specific needs and train end users myself.
fields.label_4: We're not concerned about training and learning resources. The people tasked with configuring the tool are capable of doing so without support, and end users can either be directly trained by them or are themselves highly technically proficient.

fields.title: Performance
fields.description: As certain inputs increase in whatever your use case may be‚ beneficiary counts, workflow complexities, number of tranches for cash payments, etc.‚ a tool has to be able to adapt to meet those increases. Larger volumes of data, more end users, bigger lists of cash recipients, and more can all trigger a need for a more performant solution.
fields.label_1: We're anticipating (or can't rule out) a large and potentially complex program with a number of high performance needs. We need a solution that can scale up as more records are added to the tool without greatly affecting speed, efficiency, or cost.
fields.label_2: While we are not expecting a massive, years-long use case, we still want to have the flexibility to scale up in the future without too many issues. We might need to store larger volumes of data (e.g. beneficiary photos) or accommodate more complex feature needs.
fields.label_3: We're relatively certain that we have a good sense for what our program looks like and do not anticipate the need for massively scaling up. However, we would like to keep options open for bumping up the performance should teams decide to add additional inputs.
fields.label_4: Our program is clearly-defined and we don't anticipate a huge data set or need for expandability. A lightweight solution is welcome. Our programs generally have the same volume and we do not anticipate scale up in the foreseeable future.

fields.title: Connectivity
fields.description: Connectivity in this context refers to internet access and how easily data can be sent from one place to another. Some programs or operations may be run out of a national headquarters with good connectivity, while others may be field-based and far from communications infrastructure and therefore need to adapt to an environment with poor connectivity. A disaster or crisis situation may also negatively impact connectivity, for example due to damaged telecommunications infrastructure.
fields.label_1: We need to plan for an operating environment that is extremely cutoff from telecommunications systems. The tool needs to be able to run locally on a computer without an internet connection. We expect no internet connectivity.
fields.label_2: Though the tool will be mostly used in no- or low-bandwidth environments, we will be able to periodically access the internet to upload/download data from a cloud server, but won't be able to interact with any websites in realtime. Internet may be available at very few office locations or even just a single one.
fields.label_3: We are mostly working in areas where connectivity will not be a concern, but aren't quite ready to go for a completely web-based solution. The tool will ideally store data in the cloud in order to facilitate access for end users that may be spread out, but still offer offline-functionality for certain interactions. We expect internet connectivity at multiple office locations but not everywhere the operation is taking place.
fields.label_4: Connectivity is not going to be an issue. We can consider solutions that are completely web-based and require an active and high-bandwidth internet connection. We expect internet connectivity everywhere for the program.

fields.title: Data Cleaning
fields.description: When dealing with larger datasets‚ particularly those that contain beneficiary information‚ it is common to run into data accuracy, duplication, and other issues. Some tools may offer data cleaning features, while others will require you to use separate ones to handle these matters.
fields.label_1: Given the nature of my use case, we anticipate plenty of data cleaning needs. We lack the requisite human resources to use a separate tool to handle this, so we want robust data cleaning to be part of the recommended tool's feature set. Ideally, it will catch data issues without me prompting it, and offer automatic solutions when an issue is detected.
fields.label_2: We expect there to be data cleaning needs, and would like a tool that can run reports or similar tools where our team can monitor certain data points in real-time. The criteria for these searches need to be configurable based on our needs. It's ok if we then need to manually correct the data issues that such a search catches.
fields.label_3: We don't expect my data cleaning needs to be particularly robust. We likely just need a way to identify duplicates or data entry errors, and can handle fixing those data issues on our own.
fields.label_4: Data cleaning either is not an issue we anticipate, or we will export the data to handle cleaning in a separate tool. For example, if the list of program enrollees is reviewed and provided by another organization.

fields.title: Data Extract
fields.description: Some companies and tools may rely on business models that lock users into specific ecosystems and either require you to pay to convert the data so that it can be used with other tools or simply don't allow you to migrate the data elsewhere. Interoperability in this case describes how easily you can export or reference data in the proposed solution with other tools you may wish to include as part of a suite of tools to meet your programmatic needs.
fields.label_1: We need complete flexibility with the data. Our teams will want to export data from wherever the tool is storing it into a number of other formats, including both proprietary (e.g. .xlsx, .docx) and open (e.g. .txt, .svg) formats. Data extraction must be a robust and built-in feature for the tool. The proposed solution must also have powerful data export functionality, including either a queryable API or a custom report tool.
fields.label_2: Our team will need to extract the data from the platform on a limited basis into formats that are either proprietary (e.g. .xlsx, .docx) or open (e.g. .txt, .svg), but it's acceptable if the tool manages data in such a way that not all of it can be exported. For example, if we have beneficiary lists with headshots, we would be ok with not being able to export the images and just get a CSV of the beneficiaries.
fields.label_3: Most of the work that requires access to the data can be done directly inside the proposed solution. We're not concerned about the specific formats that the data can be exported into, just that there is a way of getting data out for either analytical or archival purposes.
fields.label_4: We're not concerned about being locked into a single ecosystem, and do not anticipate needing to extract or move data from the proposed solution to another platform.

fields.title: Data Viz
fields.description: Data management tools can become rich repositories of your programmatic information, and making sense of it is much easier when you visualize it. Some tools may offer powerful features out of the box to create dynamic visualizations like maps and dashboards, while others will require you to handle data visualization on your own using other tools.
fields.label_1: Data visualization features will be extremely important to end users and audiences that will be reviewing this program. We lack the time and/or capacity to create these, and we need a tool that will offer reports via pre-built templates. We need to create graphs, charts, and maps without having technical or data visualization expertise.
fields.label_2: Data visualization features will be extremely important to end users and audiences that will be reviewing this program. We need a tool that will allow us to create data visualizations natively, but we also have the time and resources to manually configure these and do not require pre-built templates.
fields.label_3: Our team will want to visualize this data, but don't need the proposed tool to handle it for us. We need to be able to build a live connection to the data for business intelligence tools like PowerBI.
fields.label_4: We don't need data visualization as part of the tool. We are able to create any reports, dashboards, or static visualizations from manually-exported data.

fields.title: Safeguarding Data
fields.description: There are multiple challenges when collecting, storing, and using sensitive data. It is necessary to adhere to data privacy laws and regulations. Data must be protected from unauthorized access, data breaches, or theft.
fields.label_1: The program will be collecting especially sensitive data, and there may be strict regulations regarding how data is stored. We require strong data security measures for data in transit and data storage (e.g. encryption). We need control over specific user roles that limit the ways they can interact with sensitive data, and full audit logs of each action a user takes. The tool needs constantly-updated measures kept in line with evolving threats to keep hackers out. It must also pass periodic, third-party security audits.
fields.label_2: Though our program is not required to adhere to strict data regulations, we are still seeking a tool that will actively facilitate good practices around how we responsibly manage private data. Any cloud-based solution must have modern security measures in place, and the ability to limit access and read/write permissions. We expect the tool to have high-quality measures in place to unauthorized access or manipulation of the data.
fields.label_3: We will follow best practices, but are not legally required to meet any particular set of standards. The team and program are small enough that manually following best practices via internal processes will be enough. We expect to clearly define and follow data protection strategy and security policies outside of what the tool might facilitate.

fields.name: RedRose
fields.tagline: A comprehensive cash operations solution that has been widely used across the Movement.
fields.description:
Since 2015, RedRose has been widely used by numerous international organisations in over 55 countries worldwide and reached over 155 Million people. It provides a flexible and scalable system to manage all aspects of both CVA and in-kind programmes. It has been used in numerous contexts by the IFRC and ICRC since 2018.  

[youtube:https://player.vimeo.com/video/391965448?badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479]

These National Societies have also implemented RedRose:

In addition, the ICRC used RedRose in different contexts under a separate agreement.

fields.name: 121 Platform
fields.tagline: The 121 Platform is a user-friendly tool designed to streamline the Cash & Voucher Assistance (CVA) process, making it easy, safe, and fast for disaster-affected individuals to meet their own needs.
fields.description:
The 121 Platform is a user-friendly tool designed to streamline the Cash & Voucher Assistance (CVA) process, making it easy, safe, and fast. It will allow you to distribute cash in days, rather than weeks. The 121 platform is created by the Netherlands Red Cross: a platform for the movement, by the movement.

fields.name: EspoCRM - Cloud

fields.name: Excel and Kobo
fields.tagline: KoboTollbox is a free toolkit for collecting and managing data in challenging environments and is the most widely-used tool in humanitarian emergencies.
fields.description:
KoboTollbox is a free toolkit for collecting and managing data in challenging environments and is the most widely-used tool in humanitarian emergencies. The combination of kobotoolbox and Excel provide a basic system with complete data management features.

### Resources

- [IFRC FAQ](https://www.ifrc.org/ifrc-kobo)

A number of National Societies have used, and still use, the combination of Excel and Kobo for their cash programs.

IFRC Cash Data Management Officer

fields.name: AccessRC
fields.tagline: AccessRC: The mobile app for humanitarian aid
fields.description:
AccessRC is a comprehensive digital self-enrollment and program management platform that accelerates humanitarian response by providing a set of integrated tools to help a national society. With the public app, affected individuals are empowered to register, verify their eligibility, and request assistance directly through a responsive mobile app. For national societies, they utilize a web based portal for National Society staff to create programs, review and manage assistance. AccessRC enhances transparency, data quality, and operational scalability across surge operations and routine programming.  

[youtube:https://www.youtube.com/embed/wdj--Dm-oyw?si=2OU2op_CuzzA8W3C]  


### Resources

- [Homepage](https://accessrc.org/) 

### National Societies using AccessRC

Bulgaria, Colombia, Ecuador, Honduras, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Peru, Romania

### Contact

**Stephen Hagerich**  
Coordinator, Integrated Assistance  
stephen.hagerich@ifrc.org

Costs are calculated as a percantage of the CVA distributed. Setup costs are very low and as CVA programmes scale-up the costs reduce as a percentage. Helpdesk and Technical Support costs are included within the package, as well as software backups, maintenance, updates and disaster recovery.

SME's for RedRose report that the setup process takes about two full weeks for the basic installation. Setup is usually scheduled as part of a CVA or in-kind programme. During the first week the NS receives training and the RedRose system is configured and tested. During the second week an actual distribution is carried out (CVA or in-kind) by the NS. The RedRose team provide hand-holding and support during this week to ensure that the distribution is carried out correctly.

The NS receives a questionnaire to complete with details of the CVA or in-kind programme that is needed e.g. currency, fund amount, eligibiloty criteria etc. The RedRose team then configure the system based on the answers received from the NS. This simplifies the setup process for the NS, as the RedRose team provide a pre-configured system, based on the requirements of the NS.
There is no additional charge for the maintenance of the RedRose system. This includes all software updates, backups and bug-fixes.
General online training resources are available but specific training is strongly recommended for NSs.
RedRose is a highly scalable system and is capable of storing and managing millions of registration and distribution records. It performs well at scale and has been used at-scale within the RCRCM.

The RedRose OneApp (data collection and registration App) can be used offline and later synced with the main system when a connection is available. This allows for registrations and feedback forms to be completed in remote locations where there is no internet connectivity.RedRose has built-in controls for duplicate registrations/updates when used offline, to mitigate the risk of the same individual being registered multiple times when used offline.

RedRose contains various tools to help with data cleaning. Registration data is checked at the point of registration to minimise incorrect information being provided. For example, the format of phone numbers, addresses etc. are checked. There is also a duplicate checker that indicates when possible registration duplications have been entered.
There are many tools available within RedRose to filter, sort ad segment information to help with data cleansing.

Flexible data extraction. Data can be exported to a spreadsheet and also made available through an API for direct connectivity. Data can also be imported into RedRose through a very useful tool that checks for data errors when importing.
Within the RCRCM there are numerous examples of  data being imported and exported into RedRose.

A basic visual dashboard is available out-of-the-box that shows programmatic information (e.g. amount distributed, amount remaining in fund, demographic visualisations, map/geographic indicators for registrations). 
For more complete visualisations, it is recommnded that the data in RedRose is integrated with PowerBI for bespoke reporting and visualisations. This has been done for various programmes within the RCRCM.

Red Rose complies with the GDPR - a legal framework that protects the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data in the EU. GDPR compliance requires stronger protections than many other legal frameworks. Red Rose provides features that help safeguard data such as: ability to disable data exports for different users, detailed timestamped audit trails available for data creation/edits, secure backup/restore of data, and permission-based user roles/access.

The first pilot project with 121 is completely free. After that, costs are calculated as a percantage of the CVA distributed. There are no setup costs. As CVA programmes scale-up the costs reduce as a percentage. Helpdesk and Technical Support costs are included within the package, as well as software backups, maintenance, updates and disaster recovery.

Setup of a new instance will take a few hours. Configuring the instance depends on information that is shared with us by the National Society. If their registration forms and program design are ready and shared ánd they are available for potential questions, we can set up the instance in a day.

Either the project is setup by the 121 support team or users can do this themselves on the platform directly. The project will be created by importing the kobo form or the excel file used in the project. This takes no longer then 10 minutes if the kobo form or excel file is ready.

There is no additional charge for the maintenance of the 121 Platform. This includes all software updates, backups and bug-fixes. On customisation of the current tool: The 121 platform team has a close collaboration with all their partners. Since it is a movement product, users have the ability to influence the roadmap. Customisations and enhancements will be taken into account if multiple partners can benefit from it, free of charge.

The training format is a comprehensive format including 1 day how to use the platform. 1 day suffice to know how to use 121.  An additional day about CVA IM, digitalization and workflow, and finally half a day is used for practice sessions. A total of 2.5 days is required to fully adopt the 121 Platform. 
Training materials are provided at the end of the training. Most trainings are adjusted to the local team. 
An online user manual is available via the platform. 
In addition, the team can provide CVA IM trainings on Kobo and PowerBI to build further the team capacities.
The 121 platform supports projects up to 250.000 households per project. Over 15 NS have already used the 121 platform at scale!
Because the 121 platform integrates effortlessly with kobo toolbox, the offline capabilities of kobo are leveraged. The added benefit is that volunteers don't have to be re-trained.

The 121 platform supports automatic (and real-time) flagging of duplicates. Because this is clearly indicated in the platform, users can make sure to handle these duplicates before starting payments.
It further supports advanced filtering to identify missing or wrong data.
Lastly, there are automatic checks on the phoneNumber to make sure that these are entered correctly

Data can be exported (if the user role allows it) in both xlsx and csv formats.
Further; the 121 Platform API allows for integration with PowerBI and other 3rd party tools (like DEH and EspoCRM).
Data visualization is built into the 121 Platform.

The 121 platform complies with the GDPR - a legal framework that protects the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data in the EU. GDPR compliance requires stronger protections than many other legal frameworks. The 121 Platform is checked on security by a 3rd party expert twice a year.
Access to data (and exports) can be limited based on a user role. Data protection is always part of a 121 training.
All actions performed on a profile (data changes, status changes, messages, etc.) are logged, visible in the platform and can be exported for audit purposes.

EspoCRM Cloud offers a flexible pricing model where costs are based on a fixed price per user. There are no setup costs. EspoCRM Cloud support is included in the price per user. Price per user depends on the storage size of the system.

Activation can be done quickly by the vendor. Total set up time depends on complexity of the operation, but requires manual mapping of relationships between fields, establishing field types, setting user groups and permissions. All of this can be done directly in the browser and is not difficult. More complex needs, like FSP API linkages, will take time from someone with technical experience in that process.
Cloud based hosting is set up by the company as part of a subscription.
Upgrades to the system are done automatically by the developer.
Paid cloud hosting plans include dedicated email support from the developer, available during workday business hours. As a less popular tool, self-service documentation and forum support is limited.

Though not validated by the data management framework team, interviews with users of this tool report that it can slow down when record counts and cross-table queries add up. It should not be seen as a barrier, but local hosting requires consideration of your project scope as it can impact very large datasets.

Data is stored in the cloud, which means an active connection is required to access. However, the export functionality means you could download snapshots of the data to work with, so full connectivity isn't completely necessary.

No native data cleaning tools present. A reporting tool can be used for specific queries, so looking for duplicate entries is possible via a simple search, but large scale data validation and find/replace features not present without more complex workflows that either involve usage of other tools (e.g. Excel) or technical expertise.

Data is stored in CSV format and can be exported like that or in XLSX format. APIs can be connected in JSON format. Delimiters on exported data can be customized.

Should you choose to cancel EspoCRM-based Cloud hosting, you can switch to on-premise setups without any additional cost.
Good reporting functionality but limited native visualization features.

Servers are only available in Germany and Canada, so any policies related to location of servers or the transfer of PII across national borders will need to consider with that possible limitation. LDAP authentication ensures users’ permissions can be controlled, and sensitive fields can be hidden for certain user groups. Logs are maintained of all user activity. SSL Encryption (HTTPS Support) for all cloud hosted accounts.
A National Society might have access to Excel through a Microsoft subscription. If not, LibreOffice may be used at no cost. The IFRC provides all National Societies with free access to a Kobo server.
Files can be created and customized quickly with no bottlenecks.

Getting an Excel file up and running obviously requires very little technical capacity, but while the barrier to entry is low, the learning curve for taking advantage of more advanced features as a data management tool can be steep.
Assuming the file or files have been set up properly, making changes to large datasets is not difficult in Excel.
As one of the most widely used spreadsheet tools in the world, there is an abundance of available resources online, including support forums.
No description provided.
Excel files can be accessed and edited both offline and online (when stored in a cloud service like Dropbox, SharePoint, or similar).
Excel has robust features for cleaning data, but more advanced processes require a deeper understanding of the process (i.e. no "out-of-the-box" data cleaning)

The format of data stored in Excel is very interoperable and supports conversion to many other popular formats with very little skill required. When the file is stored in a cloud service like Dropbox, third party tools can be granted access to parts of—or the entire—file. However, without utilization of a cloud hosting service to store the file, creating live connections directly to the data requires a high degree of technical ability.
Tool offers decent visualization options. Essentially limitless ways to analyze the data, but like data cleaning, requires user to understand the process (i.e. does not provide automatic analysis)
No description provided.

"Core features such as launching needs assessments, PDMs, creating information only programs, and creating voucher programs are free.

Consumption based pricing occurs when launching a cash program and includes transaction fees, identity verification and other fees)"

The system is always on 24/7. Once you have access, humanitarians can rapidly launch a program (cash program or voucher program), conduct a needs assessments, or utilize the check-in features to track visits to national society facilities.
Configurable features - self-enrollment, needs assessments, information campaigns, PDMs, messaging - can be used to help manage the disaster cycle.

Access RC is governed by IFRC and member National Societies, supported by strategic private sector partnerships for technical expertise and funding. The product is continuously being updated and improved. Feedback process allows national societies to share experiences and ask for changes. If selected, enhancements are created and provided at no cost to the national society.
For training and documentation, there is an online repository with user guides, FAQs, IFRC supported learning modules, plus the option of in-country training by surge delegates.

"Access RC works for large-scale, multi-country emergencies and can also be utilized for smaller, localized preparedness, anticipatory action, response and recovery efforts.

Leverages scalable cloud infrastructure for rapid capacity adjustments and simplified updates, while retaining the choice for local hosting where required. Previous national societies have announced programs to all accounts in the country and registered 12,000 people in 24 hours."

Beneficiaries use a Android/iOS mobile app. National Society staff use a web-based portal.

Default cloud hosting can introduce performance challenges in low-connectivity regions.

AccessRC has a number data cleaning and de-dupliacation checks. We have verification levels to increase the level of assurance on identities applying for programs. When a user submits identity documents, we use an ID verification service to verify the document is real, the ID is owned by the user and matches their face. We also extract the information on the document. For documents that cannot be auto approved, we run the reviews by caseworkers to make the final decision. All this data is then utilized for de-duplication. We can check for duplicate accounts (duplication of biodata). We can also allow for configuration of de-duplication against other programs. AccessRC also has pre-payment checks that warn when batch payments are out of compliance. These prevent the double payment of individuals.
For interoperability, open APIs connect seamlessly to data management systems for end-to-end coordination.

Comprehensive built in data visualization exists with almost real time refresh. These are self-service dashboards at higher level overviews as well as program level dashboards that cover everything from applications, application processing, and assistance monitoring.

The platform supports secure ID upload via integrated vendor verification. Built with stringent data privacy and security measures - including role-based access controls and end-to-end encryption - AccessRC meets IFRC data protection standards.

Default cloud hosting can raise data-residency compliance questions - though local hosting deployments remain fully supported as an alternative.
